messages.content: 將一個2立方米的密閉室從25°C加熱到100°C，會產生多少氣體？

function.name: thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure
function.description: Calculate gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

volume.description: The volume of the chamber in cubic meters. This is a float type value.

initial_temperature.description: The initial temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

final_temperature.description: The final temperature of the gas in degree Celsius. This is a float type value.

initial_pressure.description: The initial pressure of the gas in Pascal. Default is standard atmospheric pressure. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "將一個2立方米的密閉室從25°C加熱到100°C，會產生多少氣體？" They want to know how much gas will be produced? Actually they might mean the pressure increase? The question: "將一個2立方米的密閉室從25°C加熱到100°C，會產生多少氣體？" In Chinese: "How much gas will be produced when heating a 2 cubic meter sealed chamber from 25°C to 100°C?" That seems ambiguous: maybe they want the pressure change? The phrase "產生多少氣體" literally means "how much gas will be produced". But heating a sealed chamber doesn't produce gas; it increases pressure. Maybe they want the pressure increase. So we can interpret as: calculate the gas pressure in a closed chamber due to heating. Use ideal gas law: P1V/T1 = P2V/T2 => P2 = P1 * T2/T1. T in Kelvin. So initial T=25°C=298K, final T=100°C=373K. If initial pressure is standard atmospheric pressure (101325 Pa). Then P2 = 101325 * 373/298 = 101325 * 1.2525 ≈ 126,800 Pa. So pressure increase ~25,500 Pa. So the gas pressure will be about 127 kPa. The amount of gas remains same moles. So answer: pressure ~127 kPa. If they want moles: moles = PV/RT. For initial: n = P1 V / (R T1). R=8.314 J/(mol K). So n = 101325*2/(8.314*298) ≈ 101325*2/(2477.7) ≈ 202650/2477.7 ≈ 81.8 mol. So same at final: n = P2 V / (R T2) = 126800*2/(8.314*373) ≈ 253600/(3100.9) ≈ 81.8 mol. So no change. So answer: pressure ~127 kPa. Provide explanation. Use function? We can call the function thermodynamics_calc_gas_pressure. Let's do that.
